claims.text: From the historic Terminal A Main Concourse, where St Mary's Cathedral was dedicated, to the modern Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium, witness the evolution of aviation infrastructure.
Gustave Eiffel's Air Traffic Control Tower Base stands as a testament to the airport's rich history.
Delve into the impact of connectivity and technology as seen in the transformation from the 18th-century marketplace by John Smibert to the bustling Faneuil Hall gifted by Peter Faneuil in 1742.
At the upcoming stops, you will discover the link between the airport's growth and the Air Traffic Control Tower Base, which overlooks Logan International Airport.
Additionally, you will learn about the community resistance in 1969 at the Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows.
From the Airport T station, take the escalator up to the main terminal level.
In March 1922, Boston Mayor James Michael Curley approached Massachusetts Governor Channing H. Cox with a vision for a dedicated aviation field on the tidal mudflats of Jeffries Point in East Boston.
This initiative was crucial in supporting civil commerce and national air defense, laying the groundwork for what would become Logan International Airport.
Another fascinating episode in the airport's history involves Amelia Earhart.
In 1928, she departed from Boston Airport for Newfoundland aboard the Friendship, ahead of her historic transatlantic flight.
This moment marked a pivotal achievement in aviation history and cemented Boston's role as a key player in the development of international air travel.
The Terminal A Main Concourse not only embodies sustainable design but also echoes the innovative spirit of early aviation pioneers.

As you approach the Air Traffic Control Tower Base, you'll find yourself standing in the shadow of a monumental structure that has overseen the rhythms of Logan International Airport since its construction in 1973.
Look up to see the Brutalist concrete design, a signature of architects Perry, Dean, Stahl & Rogers, marking a pivotal evolution in airport architecture.
The tower's history is intertwined with the growth of Logan International Airport, which spans over 2,384 acres and handles more than 43.5 million passengers annually.
On April 23, 1969, the Massachusetts Port Authority cleared to extend Runway 15R/33L, resulting in the removal of dozens of historic mature trees.
This stop connects to the broader theme of the tour, highlighting Logan Airport as a hub of innovation and history, where the skies above are navigated with precision and care.
Here, the runways stretch over a landscape that once housed Wood Island Park.
The transformation of this land set the stage for community resistance in 1969, as neighborhood mothers boldly blocked dump trucks with baby carriages.
Charles Lindbergh and Amelia Earhart once soared above this very site, leaving their mark on the annals of history.

claims.text: Originally known as Jeffery Field, Boston Airport officially opened on September 8, 1923, primarily serving the U.S. Army Air Service and the Massachusetts National Guard.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: A significant historical event linked to this airport occurred on July 22, 1927, when the pioneering aviator Charles Lindbergh landed the Spirit of St. Louis here.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: After his historic solo transatlantic flight, Lindbergh embarked on a national tour to promote aviation.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: His arrival at Logan was met by tens of thousands who gathered to see the man who had crossed the Atlantic nonstop.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: This event marked a milestone in aviation history and highlighted the airport's emerging role in connecting America to the world.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: The transformation of Terminal E reflects a commitment to innovation and progress, echoing the spirit of those early days of aviation.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: The modernization project has expanded Logan's capacity and enhanced the passenger experience, aligning with the airport's legacy of connecting Boston to the global community.

claims.stop: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium
claims.text: This stop, like the Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows you visited earlier, opens a window into the world of aviation, reminding us of the strides made since the days of Lindbergh.
